title: Write server timestamps for LWW ordering fields in FirestoreGatewayImpl's push* methods (FB-2)

evidence.quote: Every cross-device LWW ordering field is written as `FieldValue.serverTimestamp()`, never a client clock.

the device with the
strictly newer timestamp wins.
// remote document carries a valid LWW timestamp. The merger

why: docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md names `updatedAt` as the LWW comparison field for curriculum_tracks, goals, bookmarks and settings. pushTrack (line 337), pushSettings (316), pushBookmark (369) and pushGoal (562) all spread the caller's `data` -- which carries whatever client-clock `updated_at` the local write set -- straight through, and only add a separate `synced_at: FieldValue.serverTimestamp()` field that isn't the one the merger compares. pushLearnerProfile (line 417) shows the codebase already knows the right pattern: it explicitly overwrites `updated_at` itself with `FieldValue.serverTimestamp()` before sending. FB-2's own stated rationale is exact: 'two devices with skewed clocks writing client timestamps make last-write-wins non-deterministic -- the faster clock always wins and silently overwrites newer data.' A device with a fast or wrong clock editing a track/goal/bookmark/setting can have its stale edit incorrectly beat a genuinely later edit from another device, with the loss silent (no error, just the wrong value persisting until the next edit).
recommendation: Apply the pushLearnerProfile pattern (server-side overwrite of the merger's LWW field) to pushTrack, pushSettings, pushBookmark, pushGoal and any other push* method whose entity is LWW-merged by a client-set timestamp field; confirm against core/sync/merge/*.dart which exact field each merger compares before changing it.
acceptance_criteria: Emulator test (per FB-2's own 'Enforce' note) asserts the persisted field each merger actually compares is a server Timestamp, not a client-supplied value, for tracks/goals/bookmarks/settings.
Audit grep: no client-clock value reaches a field a merger uses for cross-device LWW comparison, across firestore_gateway_impl.dart's push* methods.

corrections: Two inaccuracies to correct, neither defeats the finding: (1) the docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md quote is real text but sits at lines 17-18, not line 16 (line 16 is the stage_definitions row). (2) The finding's 'why' says the doc names updatedAt as curriculum_tracks' LWW field, but the doc actually says max(activatedAt, deactivatedAt) and the live code (track_codec.dart, firestore_listener_source.dart:80) uses state_changed_at, not updated_at, for tracks. The same defect pattern still applies to pushTrack (it passes state_changed_at through unmodified), so the site count/recommendation stands but the field name for tracks in the writeup should read 'state_changed_at' not 'updatedAt'.

Two corrections, neither fatal to the finding: (1) docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md quote is actually at lines 17-18, not line 16 (off-by-one). (2) The finding's "why" overstates the gap slightly — the merger DOES read/compare `synced_at`, but only as a secondary tie-breaker within a ±5s clock-skew window (see DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer); outside that window it falls back to the unmodified client `updated_at`. The core defect (client clock reaches the field used for the dominant comparison branch, contra FB-2) still holds for skew beyond 5s.
None needed — all cited file:line quotes verified verbatim against the current tree.

mergedFrom: Sync push payloads embed client-clock timestamps as the cross-device LWW ordering field instead of FieldValue.serverTimestamp()
